headline: High: firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling can feed social-auto-upload’s account workflows, creating leakage and compliance risk; prompt-injection and conflict risks are lower but present via shared content handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API outputs, while social-auto-upload consumes media/account workflows from files and CLI. A shared content bridge is plausible if firecrawl output is copied into upload inputs, so attacker-controlled page text could influence downstream actions. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is copied into social-auto-upload input files or captions without sanitization, prompt content can propagate.
IF either agent treats fetched web text as instructions, injected instructions may be followed.
mitigations: Sanitize and strip instructions from scraped text before reuse.
Use a fixed template for captions and metadata.
Review one sample handoff manually before bulk runs.
Keep firecrawl and upload inputs in separate folders.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: firecrawl handles API keys and broad network egress, while social-auto-upload touches account data and local media files. If firecrawl output or logs are reused in upload workflows, sensitive structured data or screenshots could leak into social-media content or third-party endpoints. The pair lacks a documented shared workspace, so this is inferred but credible.
conditions: IF firecrawl outputs include API keys, screenshots, or structured data and are forwarded into social-auto-upload inputs, leakage occurs.
IF both agents are run under the same account or workspace, cross-contamination becomes possible.
mitigations: Redact secrets before any handoff.
Store upload assets in a separate directory from crawl outputs.
Check one generated post for accidental sensitive fields.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: firecrawl can make broad network requests and supports multiple instances; social-auto-upload also has broad egress and multiple-instance support, but it cannot write files, modify git, or run shells. Overlap is mainly network-side, so direct resource contention is limited and the blast radius is small compared with filesystem or git conflicts.
conditions: IF both agents target the same external API quota or account simultaneously, request contention can occur.
IF an operator reuses the same credentials across both agents, rate-limit conflicts may surface.
mitigations: Stagger runs by a few minutes.
Use separate API keys or accounts.
Set per-agent rate limits.
Monitor quota usage during the first run.
requires-engineering: add a shared lock for external API calls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data that social-auto-upload could plausibly turn into posts or media metadata. Because social-auto-upload is an action-taking uploader, any unverified firecrawl output can cascade into public-facing mistakes. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is used as source text for captions or descriptions without review, incorrect facts can be published.
IF social-auto-upload is pointed at generated assets from firecrawl, downstream posting errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require a human review step before posting.
Compare one post against the source page manually.
Limit automation to drafts first.
Keep a rollback plan for mistaken posts.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for source-to-post transformations.

E_compliance.rationale: firecrawl explicitly handles API keys and broad egress, while social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads to social platforms. If EU or regulated content is scraped by firecrawl and then posted or stored by social-auto-upload, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is scraped by firecrawl and later uploaded by social-auto-upload, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention policies differ between crawl artifacts and uploaded account data, deletion requests may fail end-to-end.
mitigations: Avoid scraping regulated personal data.
Delete crawl artifacts after use.
Document retention for both agents.
Confirm platform-specific posting policies before automation.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems.
